name: Eye foreign body and corneal abrasion (includes chemical splash to the eye)
likelihood_per_mission_or_per_person_yea: 0.722 probability of at least one event per crew member, 6 month LEO mission, 1 EVA (IMM model output)
severity: 3 (can threaten sight; eye chemical burn is a modeled evacuation driver)
red_flags: Object stuck in the eye; any chemical in the eye; any change in vision (blurred or double); eye painful and red; nausea or headache with eye pain; bleeding that will not stop
tests_possible_onboard: Pain score (painScore); visual acuity each eye with the ISS eye chart (no equipment id, not in equipment.json); no fluorescein or slit lamp step for a layperson found
rank_reason: High likelihood plus a sight threat; floating debris is the most recorded eye event on Shuttle and ISS.
source_title: Ranking of Medical Conditions by Probability (NASA IMM Data Request Report, iMED v5.0, dated 2 Feb 2015, linked from NASA IMM Overview page)
source_section: Table 2: Six month Low Earth Orbit with 1 EVA, p2 (probability of at least one event, one crew member)
plain: Something in your eye or a scratch on it. Do not rub it. Chemicals or a stuck object are an emergency.
severity_basis_quote: In one assessment, Eye Chemical Burn was the top influential medical condition contributing to the probability of evacuation for certain ISS mission conditions
red_flags_section: When to Contact a Medical Professional
red_flags_quote: There appears to be a scratch, cut, or something has gone into (penetrated) the eyeball.
notes: Meer 2023 reports 70 of 104 ocular events in LSAH records were eye abrasion from a foreign body (Shuttle and ISS to Expedition 13). Supporting quote (Meer; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41526-023-00279-y): "There were 70 corneal abrasions, 4 dry eyes, 4 eye debris, 5 complaints of ocular irritation, 6 chemical burns"

name: Space motion sickness (space adaptation)
likelihood_per_mission_or_per_person_yea: 0.730 probability per crew member, 6 month LEO (IMM); OCHMO brief says up to 73% of crew in first 2-3 days
severity: 2 (can stop work; vomiting causes dehydration; EVA delayed)
red_flags: More than 2 vomiting episodes; symptoms beyond 72 hours; clear drop in performance; cannot keep fluids down; blood or coffee-ground material in vomit
tests_possible_onboard: heartRate and BP (eq-bp-monitor, eq-manual-pulse); temperatureC (eq-thermometer-oral); electrolytes if vomiting (eq-pcba-istat, EC6+ cartridge); auscultation (eq-stethoscope)
rank_reason: Most common early-flight problem; vomiting in a closed cabin or suit and dehydration make it more than a nuisance.
source_title: Ranking of Medical Conditions by Probability (NASA IMM Data Request Report, iMED v5.0, dated 2 Feb 2015, linked from NASA IMM Overview page)
source_section: Table 2: Six month Low Earth Orbit with 1 EVA, p2 (probability of at least one event, one crew member)
plain: Feeling sick from weightlessness. Keep your head still. Vomiting many times is serious.
severity_basis_quote: Concerns include health decrements (dehydration and weakness) and decreased crew performance.
red_flags_source_title: OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A, Space Adaptation Sickness (SAS) and Space Readaptation Syndrome, NASA-STD-3001 Medical Technical Brief (09/25/2025)
red_flags_section: Pathophysiology, SMS Grading Criteria table, Severe (3), p6
red_flags_quote: includes more than 2 episodes of vomiting; significant performance decrement may be apparent; symptoms may persist beyond 72 hours
notes: MTB-004 p4 lists diagnosis capabilities: auscultation device and blood analysis (check electrolytes if vomiting). Supporting quote (OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A; https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/ochmo-mtb-004-space-adaptation-sickness-sas.pdf): "Capabilities needed for diagnosis: Auscultation device, blood analysis (check electrolytes if vomiting)"

name: Headache in flight (space adaptation, late, and CO2-induced)
likelihood_per_mission_or_per_person_yea: Late headache 0.592, space adaptation headache 0.351, CO2-induced headache 0.306 per crew member, 6 month LEO (IMM)
severity: 2 (usually not dangerous; CO2 headache signals a cabin air problem for all crew; some red flags mean stroke or bleeding in the brain)
red_flags: Sudden explosive headache; worst headache ever; slurred speech, vision change, weakness, loss of balance or confusion; fever with stiff neck; headache after a head injury; headache worse over 24 hours
tests_possible_onboard: painScore; temperatureC (eq-thermometer-oral); systolicBP/diastolicBP/heartRate (eq-bp-monitor); cabin CO2 reading from vehicle sensors (no measurement key exists)
rank_reason: Very common, and the card can catch two dangerous things: a CO2 problem that affects everyone, and rare brain emergencies.
source_title: Ranking of Medical Conditions by Probability (NASA IMM Data Request Report, iMED v5.0, dated 2 Feb 2015, linked from NASA IMM Overview page)
source_section: Table 2: Six month Low Earth Orbit with 1 EVA, p2 (probability of at least one event, one crew member)
plain: Headache is common in space. A sudden, very bad headache, or trouble speaking or seeing, is an emergency.
severity_basis_section: Background, anecdotal CO2 symptom associations, p4
severity_basis_quote: Headaches at levels between 2.8-4.5 mmHg; worsening with increasing levels of CO2 accompanied by fatigue and malaise flushing.
red_flags_section: When to Contact a Medical Professional
red_flags_quote: Your headache comes on suddenly and is explosive or violent. This kind of headache needs medical attention right away.
notes: van Oosterhout 2024: 22 of 24 ISS astronauts had at least one headache in flight. TB-004: 19 of 49 astronauts reported headaches in an ISS CO2 study. Supporting quote (OCHMO-TB-004 Rev D; https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/ochmo-tb-004-carbon-dioxide.pdf): "19 of the 49 astronauts reported experiencing headaches (~38.7%)."

name: Choking or obstructed airway
likelihood_per_mission_or_per_person_yea: 0.0533 probability per crew member, 6 month LEO (IMM)
red_flags: Cannot speak; difficulty breathing; noisy or high-pitched breathing; weak cough; bluish skin; becomes unresponsive
tests_possible_onboard: oxygenSat (eq-blood-oximeter); heartRate (eq-manual-pulse). Microgravity method for back blows or abdominal thrusts: NOT FOUND (searched OCHMO briefs, HRP 2017 evidence report, Hinkelbein 2020)
rank_reason: Rare but kills in minutes, so the ground cannot help in time; the card must stand alone.

plain: If they cannot talk or breathe, act now. Do not wait for the ground.
severity_basis_quote: Loss of consciousness (unresponsiveness) if the blockage is not cleared
red_flags_source_title: MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia (NLM), Choking - adult or child over 1 year
red_flags_quote: look for these danger signs: Inability to speak Difficulty breathing
notes: Earth first aid assumes gravity and a standing rescuer. Microgravity technique not found in public sources.

name: Fire, smoke inhalation and burns
likelihood_per_mission_or_per_person_yea: Smoke inhalation 0.0112, burns secondary to fire 0.00526 per crew member, 6 month LEO (IMM; model-derived, not observed events)
red_flags: Breathed in smoke; burn the size of a palm or larger; full-thickness burn; burn from chemicals or electricity; signs of shock
tests_possible_onboard: oxygenSat (eq-blood-oximeter); heartRate and BP (eq-bp-monitor); painScore. Pulse oximeter accuracy after smoke: NOT FOUND in sources read
rank_reason: Low modeled probability but a whole-crew life threat; brief lists fire and toxic atmosphere as always required.

plain: Fire or smoke: get clean air first. Then check burns and breathing.
severity_basis_quote: combustion products can present an immediate threat to the life of the crew due to the limited escape options
red_flags_section: When to Contact a Medical Professional

name: Skin abrasion, laceration and bleeding
likelihood_per_mission_or_per_person_yea: Skin abrasion 0.821, skin laceration 0.0181 per crew member, 6 month LEO (IMM)
red_flags: Bleeding cannot be controlled; wound may need stitches; dirt cannot be cleaned out; signs of internal bleeding or shock; signs of infection
tests_possible_onboard: heartRate, systolicBP (eq-bp-monitor); painScore; temperatureC for infection (eq-thermometer-oral)
rank_reason: Second most likely event in the model; severe bleeding is on the brief always-list.

severity_basis_quote: You think there may be internal bleeding or shock.

likelihood_per_mission_or_per_person_yea: Skin rash 0.821, allergic reaction (mild to moderate) 0.182, anaphylaxis 0.000245 per crew member, 6 month LEO (IMM)
red_flags: Difficulty breathing, wheeze or high-pitched breathing; swelling of face, eyes or tongue; very hoarse or whispered voice; dizziness; unconsciousness
rank_reason: Rash is the most reported ISS event; anaphylaxis is rare but fatal fast and is on the brief always-list.

plain: A rash is common. Swelling of the face or trouble breathing is an emergency.
severity_basis_quote: Anaphylaxis is an emergency condition that needs medical attention right away.
red_flags_quote: A warning sign of dangerous throat swelling is a very hoarse or whispered voice, or coarse sounds when the person is breathing in air.
notes: Crucian 2016: skin rashes were the most reported event at 1.12 per flight year in 46 ISS long-duration crew. Supporting quote (Crucian et al. 2016; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5098747/): "Skin rashes were the most reported event (1.12/flight year)"

name: Back pain (space adaptation) and back injury
likelihood_per_mission_or_per_person_yea: Space adaptation back pain 0.525, back injury 0.443 per crew member, 6 month LEO (IMM); 52% in first 2-5 days (OCHMO)
severity: 1 for adaptation back pain; 2 for injury
red_flags: Loss of control of urine or stool; weakness or numbness in buttocks, thigh, leg or pelvis; pain after a hard blow; fever with back pain; pain down the leg below the knee
rank_reason: Very common; card is mostly reassurance plus spinal red flags.

name: Urinary retention and urinary tract infection
likelihood_per_mission_or_per_person_yea: Urinary retention 0.00697 (male) and 0.0556 (female); UTI 0.0811 (male) and 0.490 (female) per crew member, 6 month LEO (IMM)
severity: 2 (3 if infection spreads; urosepsis is a modeled evacuation driver)
red_flags: Cannot pass urine; fever; back or side pain; blood in urine
rank_reason: Documented in flight and needs a catheter skill; untreated it can lead to sepsis.

red_flags: Joint pain after EVA or pressure change; stroke-like symptoms; loss of consciousness; seizure; cough and shortness of breath
rank_reason: Tied to a planned activity, can be catastrophic, and needs a fast specific response.

rank_reason: Low probability but a top evacuation driver, and bone loss in flight raises the risk.
